findings.title: Abundance pressures valuation without creating equality
findings.claim: The focus quantity phrase can make abundance a pressure on judgment without making quantity a measure of worth.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier كَثْرَةُ names numerical abundance and is joined to the focus form of admiration; the supplied wider targets then show corrupt accumulation being separated, passing residue being distinguished from what benefits, and majority being unable to establish soundness. Those contacts make the negated equality an audit of quantity-driven valuation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why impressive amount affects attention while leaving the qualitative distinction intact.
findings.containment: This retains the focus claim that bad and good are not equal. It does not make abundance intrinsically bad, and it omits the unresolved purified-intellect branch.

epistemic.reason: The bounded core is supported by an accepted focus branch and a legacy reader walk; the wider connection targets supply Arabic and notes but not target morphology, so the global extension remains qualified.

branch_activations.boundary: The activation does not condemn every abundance and does not claim the unresolved l-b-b branch as an independent lexical reading.

findings.title: Admiration is exposed as a pressure on valuation
findings.claim: The focus concessive clause makes being pleased by an appearance part of the judgment under examination, while wider supplied examples keep admiration from becoming a verdict on worth.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier أَعْجَبَكَ names caused admiration; the supplied targets connect beautified accumulation, displayed numbers, Qarun's admired display, and near-life adornment with unreliable or temporary valuation. The contact changes the clause from a passing concession into an explicit test of the eye's measure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that the ayah examines the evaluator's attraction as well as the objects being compared.
findings.containment: Admiration remains a real perceptual response in the focus reading. The finding does not claim that everything pleasant is bad or that visual appeal has no human effect.

findings.title: Abundance is classified by quality, function, and response
